It is well known that SIBs possess further potential application in extreme cold conditions than LIBs owing to its high capacity retention and rate performance at low temperature $[17]$ . The following test focused on the effect of NaDFP at the low temperature performance of the battery. Capacities of batteries without NaDFP sharply drop owing to the low coulombic efficiency and capacity retention only remains 50 % after 100 cycles, while the battery using 1 wt% NaDFP electrolyte shows better cycle stability and capacity retention remains 90 % after 100 cycles. Fig. 3b and 3c show the curves of $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ cycle. SIBs with and without NaDFP have similar charging and discharging starting points (about 2.4 V &3.5 V) at the initial stage of the cycle. However, as the reaction progresses, the polarization of the batteries without NaDFP became more and more serious, and abruptly lost much of their capacities in a rollover fashion (“Sudden death”) after 100 cycles. Comparing the rate performance shown in Fig. 3d, batteries with NaDFP hold higher capacity retention at each rate. Notably, capacity gap at low temperature between batteries with and without additives is much larger than that of room temperature. Further evaluating battery performance under extreme conditions, $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ discharge test were followed.

3.1. Design and properties of the dual-additive electrolytes
The basic criteria for designing a functional electrolyte of SIBs with wide-temperature performance are illustrated in Fig. 1a and b. In general, low conductivity, high viscosity and sluggish charge transfer processes, which resulting from high energy barriers for $Na^{+}$ desolvation and $Na^{+}$ migration in the SEI, are the main factors that limit the SIBs low-temperature performance [20]. And with the improving temperature, the increase of side reactions and ion dissolution will gradually become the causes of performance degradation [21]. As mentioned above [22], NaDFP can serve as a film-forming additive, the NaDFP-containing functional electrolyte greatly improves the pouch SIBs performance, but the inferior physical properties including lower conductivity, higher viscosity, and instability at extreme conditions still need to be solved. Therefore, combined with the synthesis of NaDFP shown in Fig. 1c, two functional electrolytes are designed by “hard-soft synergy” strategy and evaluated under tough temperature conditions. Namely, 1 % NaDFP is respectively coupled with 1.5 % TMSP and 1.5 % TMSB as the co-additive of two functional electrolytes. It is expected that the functional groups and elemental composition of additives can be used to form a synergistic effect, in order to optimize the film-forming quality of electrode and solvation structure of electrolyte, leading to wonderful wide-temperature performance of SIBs.

The HOMO energies and LUMO energies of $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP, TMSB and other solvents were first calculated using DFT method to assess their stability and reactive feasibility as the components of electrolyte, as shown in Fig. 1d. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

source_refs.raw_quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.chunk_id: 0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0
citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.chunk_id: 0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9
citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ .

3.1. Design and properties of the dual-additive electrolytes
The basic criteria for designing a functional electrolyte of SIBs with wide-temperature performance are illustrated in Fig. 1a and b. In general, low conductivity, high viscosity and sluggish charge transfer processes, which resulting from high energy barriers for $Na^{+}$ desolvation and $Na^{+}$ migration in the SEI, are the main factors that limit the SIBs low-temperature performance [20]. And with the improving temperature, the increase of side reactions and ion dissolution will gradually become the causes of performance degradation [21]. As mentioned above [22], NaDFP can serve as a film-forming additive, the NaDFP-containing functional electrolyte greatly improves the pouch SIBs performance, but the inferior physical properties including lower conductivity, higher viscosity, and instability at extreme conditions still need to be solved. Therefore, combined with the synthesis of NaDFP shown in Fig. 1c, two functional electrolytes are designed by “hard-soft synergy” strategy and evaluated under tough temperature conditions. Namely, 1 % NaDFP is respectively coupled with 1.5 % TMSP and 1.5 % TMSB as the co-additive of two functional electrolytes. It is expected that the functional groups and elemental composition of additives can be used to form a synergistic effect, in order to optimize the film-forming quality of electrode and solvation structure of electrolyte, leading to wonderful wide-temperature performance of SIBs.

The HOMO energies and LUMO energies of $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP, TMSB and other solvents were first calculated using DFT method to assess their stability and reactive feasibility as the components of electrolyte, as shown in Fig. 1d. citations.quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.quote:
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

requirements.reasoning: Cai 2025 报告 NFM/HC 软包电池在 -10 °C、1C 下 NB 电解液的倍率性能改善，并明确含 NB 电解液的电池“更适于低温应用”，与目标电芯化学和温度一致。

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3
citations.quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

requirements.requirement: 对 Al 集流体无腐蚀（阴性事实）
requirements.reasoning: Fan 2025 只在电解槽/扣式电池中显示无添加剂的 NaPF6-E 几乎不与 Al 箔反应，并未测试含 NaDFP/TMSB 的 NB 电解液，也未在目标软包构型中直接观察；Cai 2025 未涉及腐蚀测试，故不能证明候选电解液对 Al 无腐蚀。

citations.chunk_id: 0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9::child0
citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ .

requirements.requirement: 对不锈钢壳体无腐蚀（阴性事实）

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

evidence_ledger.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

evidence_ledger.quote:
ABSTRACT
An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

The following test focused on the effect of NaDFP at the low temperature performance of the battery. Capacities of batteries without NaDFP sharply drop owing to the low coulombic efficiency and capacity retention only remains 50 % after 100 cycles, while the battery using 1 wt% NaDFP electrolyte shows better cycle stability and capacity retention remains 90 % after 100 cycles. Fig. 3b and 3c show the curves of $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ cycle. SIBs with and without NaDFP have similar charging and discharging starting points (about 2.4 V &3.5 V) at the initial stage of the cycle. However, as the reaction progresses, the polarization of the batteries without NaDFP became more and more serious, and abruptly lost much of their capacities in a rollover fashion (“Sudden death”) after 100 cycles. Comparing the rate performance shown in Fig. 3d, batteries with NaDFP hold higher capacity retention at each rate. Notably, capacity gap at low temperature between batteries with and without additives is much larger than that of room temperature. Further evaluating battery performance under extreme conditions, $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ discharge test were followed.

3.1. Design and properties of the dual-additive electrolytes
The basic criteria for designing a functional electrolyte of SIBs with wide-temperature performance are illustrated in Fig. 1a and b. 3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

association_citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

3.1. Design and properties of the dual-additive electrolytes
The basic criteria for designing a functional electrolyte of SIBs with wide-temperature performance are illustrated in Fig. 1a and b. In general, low conductivity, high viscosity and sluggish charge transfer processes, which resulting from high energy barriers for $Na^{+}$ desolvation and $Na^{+}$ migration in the SEI, are the main factors that limit the SIBs low-temperature performance [20]. And with the improving temperature, the increase of side reactions and ion dissolution will gradually become the causes of performance degradation [21]. As mentioned above [22], NaDFP can serve as a film-forming additive, the NaDFP-containing functional electrolyte greatly improves the pouch SIBs performance, but the inferior physical properties including lower conductivity, higher viscosity, and instability at extreme conditions still need to be solved. Therefore, combined with the synthesis of NaDFP shown in Fig. 1c, two functional electrolytes are designed by “hard-soft synergy” strategy and evaluated under tough temperature conditions. Namely, 1 % NaDFP is respectively coupled with 1.5 % TMSP and 1.5 % TMSB as the co-additive of two functional electrolytes. citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

citations.quote: The rate capability of the battery containing NaDFP was obviously improved at each current. Fig. 2c shows the cycling performance of the electrolyte with and without NaDFP. Obviously, the capacity was improved with the adding of the NaDFP. The capacity of the batteries using the baseline electrolyte gradually decline after 500 cycles. Oppositely, cycling stability was significantly improved by adding NaDFP, and the battery using 1 wt% NaDFP electrolyte have the highest cycle stability remaining 90 % capacity retention after 700 cycles, while battery using baseline electrolyte capacity retention only remains 70 %. Fig. 2e and 2f show the charge/discharge curves during cycling. It can be noticed that the capacity fading of battery with baseline electrolyte is mainly caused by the increasing polarization. This polarization is probably due to the continuous electrolyte reduction and deposition on electrode surface. In the contrast, the polarization of battery with 1.0 wt % NaDFP-containing electrolyte was less pronounced compared to the baseline electrolyte, resulting in a much-improved cycling stability.

It is well known that SIBs possess further potential application in extreme cold conditions than LIBs owing to its high capacity retention and rate performance at low temperature $[17]$ . The following test focused on the effect of NaDFP at the low temperature performance of the battery. Capacities of batteries without NaDFP sharply drop owing to the low coulombic efficiency and capacity retention only remains 50 % after 100 cycles, while the battery using 1 wt% NaDFP electrolyte shows better cycle stability and capacity retention remains 90 % after 100 cycles. Fig. 3b and 3c show the curves of $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ cycle. SIBs with and without NaDFP have similar charging and discharging starting points (about 2.4 V &3.5 V) at the initial stage of the cycle. However, as the reaction progresses, the polarization of the batteries without NaDFP became more and more serious, and abruptly lost much of their capacities in a rollover fashion (“Sudden death”) after 100 cycles. Comparing the rate performance shown in Fig. 3d, batteries with NaDFP hold higher capacity retention at each rate. Notably, capacity gap at low temperature between batteries with and without additives is much larger than that of room temperature. Further evaluating battery performance under extreme conditions, $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ discharge test were followed.

3.1. Design and properties of the dual-additive electrolytes
The basic criteria for designing a functional electrolyte of SIBs with wide-temperature performance are illustrated in Fig. 1a and b. In general, low conductivity, high viscosity and sluggish charge transfer processes, which resulting from high energy barriers for $Na^{+}$ desolvation and $Na^{+}$ migration in the SEI, are the main factors that limit the SIBs low-temperature performance [20]. And with the improving temperature, the increase of side reactions and ion dissolution will gradually become the causes of performance degradation [21]. As mentioned above [22], NaDFP can serve as a film-forming additive, the NaDFP-containing functional electrolyte greatly improves the pouch SIBs performance, but the inferior physical properties including lower conductivity, higher viscosity, and instability at extreme conditions still need to be solved. Therefore, combined with the synthesis of NaDFP shown in Fig. 1c, two functional electrolytes are designed by “hard-soft synergy” strategy and evaluated under tough temperature conditions. Namely, 1 % NaDFP is respectively coupled with 1.5 % TMSP and 1.5 % TMSB as the co-additive of two functional electrolytes. It is expected that the functional groups and elemental composition of additives can be used to form a synergistic effect, in order to optimize the film-forming quality of electrode and solvation structure of electrolyte, leading to wonderful wide-temperature performance of SIBs.

First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

### 候选资料：c1-napf6-ec-emc-1wt-tmsbs（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：TMSBS；添加剂用量：TMSBS=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

## 候选评估
### c1-napf6-ec-emc-1wt-tmsbs
评估建议：The candidate matches source 0031's NFM/HC pouch electrolyte (NaPF6 1 M, EC:EMC 3:7, 1 wt% TMSBS) with demonstrated -10 C operation and NaPF6's non-corrosion of Al, but the program's hard requirement of no stainless-steel shell corrosion is not supported by direct negative evidence for this electrolyte, so a held decision is warranted pending that confirmation.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Salt is NaPF6 at ~1.0 mol/L concentration：Source 0031 explicitly prepares a 1 mol L^-1 NaPF6 baseline electrolyte, matching the candidate's salt and concentration. [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]
- Solvent is EC:EMC = 3:7 on a mass basis：Source 0031 states NaPF6 was dissolved into EC:EMC = 3:7 in wt%, matching the candidate's mass-basis 30/70 ratio. [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]
- Additive is 1 wt% TMSBS：Source 0031 adds TMSBS additive (1 wt%) to the baseline to form the functional electrolyte, matching the candidate. [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]
- Cell format is NFM||hard-carbon pouch：Source 0031 assembles pouch NFM/HC cells with this electrolyte, matching the requested cell chemistry and format. [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]
- Operates at low temperature (-10 C)：Source 0031 reports -10 C cycling and rate performance of pouch NFM/HC cells with the TMSBS-containing electrolyte, directly covering the target low-temperature condition. [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec7::child2]
- No observed Al current-collector corrosion：Source 0016 reports Al foil corrosion results in different electrolytes and states NaPF6-E hardly reacts, giving a direct negative observation for the NaPF6-based electrolyte on Al. [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9]
- No observed stainless-steel shell corrosion：Source 0016 only establishes stainless-steel shell corrosion for NaFSI-E ('corrode stainless steel first'); it provides no direct negative observation that the NaPF6-based electrolyte leaves the stainless-steel shell intact. [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate composition is identical to the functional electrolyte of source 0031 (NaPF6 1 mol/L in EC:EMC 3:7 wt% plus 1 wt% TMSBS) tested in NFM/HC pouch cells at low temperature, so the performance association is direct; the corrosion association comes from source 0016 Fan, whose NaPF6-based electrolyte is the same salt family, but its stainless-steel result is reported only for NaFSI-E. [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0][0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9]
### c2-napf6-ec-emc-1wt-nadfp
评估建议：The candidate is well supported as a low-temperature formulation: its exact composition matches the 0.8 M NaPF6/EC:EMC 3:7 + 1 wt% NaDFP electrolyte that Cai 2024 cycled in NFM/HC pouch cells at -10 °C, and Fan 2025 gives an Al-foil non-corrosion observation for NaPF6-E. However, the program's hard requirement of no observed stainless-steel-shell corrosion is not directly evidenced for this NaPF6-based electrolyte (only NaFSI-E shell corrosion is reported), so a recommendation is held pending that specific negative observation.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Salt identity and concentration: NaPF6 at 0.8 mol/L：Cai 2024 prepares the baseline by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7, and Fan 2025 also uses 0.8 M NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7, matching the candidate salt and concentration. [0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0][0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec5::child0]
- Solvent system: EC:EMC = 3:7：Both sources state the electrolyte is a mixture of EC:EMC = 3:7, matching the candidate solvent ratio. [0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0][0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec5::child0]
- Additive: 1 wt% NaDFP：Cai 2024 states that saturation of NaDFP in 0.8 M NaPF6-EC/EMC occurs above 1 wt% and that 1 wt% is the optimal additive concentration giving the highest capacity retention and rate capacity. [0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec7::child5]
- Low-temperature operation at -10 °C in an NFM||hard-carbon pouch cell：Cai 2024 reports NFM/HC pouch cells with 1 wt% NaDFP retaining ~90% capacity at -10 °C versus only 50% for the additive-free baseline, and describes the -10 °C cycling and rate behavior of these pouch cells. [0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec7::child7]
- Cell format is a pouch cell with Al current collector：Cai 2024 assembles NFM/HC pouch cells with slurries coated on an aluminum substrate; Fan 2025 also builds pouch cells. Thus the Al current collector and pouch format are explicitly represented. [0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0][0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec5]
- No observed Al current-collector corrosion：Fan 2025 reports Al-foil corrosion results for different salts and states that NaDFOB-E and NaPF6-E hardly react, i.e. a direct negative observation for the NaPF6-based electrolyte on Al. [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9::child0]
- No observed stainless-steel shell corrosion for this NaPF6-based electrolyte：Fan 2025 reports obvious shell corrosion traces only for NaFSI-E (inferring NaFSI corrodes Al and stainless steel, stainless steel first); it gives no direct negative observation for the NaPF6-E electrolyte on a stainless-steel shell, so the required corrosion-free shell fact is not established for this candidate. [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9::child0]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate formulation (0.8 M NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7 with 1 wt% NaDFP) reproduces the electrolyte of Cai 2024, which was actually cycled in NFM/HC pouch cells at -10 °C (about 90% retention for the additive-containing cell versus 50% for baseline) and characterized for SEI/interfacial stability; the Al-substrate electrode fabrication in the same paper associates the candidate with an Al current collector. Corrosion behavior is associated only through Fan 2025, which measured Al-foil and stainless-steel-shell corrosion for NaPF6-E, NaFSI-E and NaDFOB-E in pouch/coin configurations; the Al-foil negative result supports the collector requirement for NaPF6-E, while the stainless-steel-shell negative result is not reported for NaPF6-E. [0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec7::child7][0152_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0][0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9::child0]
### c3-napf6-ec-emc-nadfp-tmsb
评估建议：候选与 Cai 2025 的 NB 电解液在盐/溶剂/浓度/添加剂上一致，且该体系在 NFM/HC 软包电池 -10 °C 下显示低温优势，低温性能要求得到文献支持；但项目硬性要求“未观察到集流体或壳体腐蚀”缺乏针对该含添加剂候选的直接阴性证据，故暂不推荐，建议补充候选电解液在 Al 及不锈钢壳上的腐蚀验证后再决定。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- NaPF6 盐在 EC:EMC = 3:7 溶剂中配成 0.8 mol/L 基础电解液：Cai 2025 明确基线电解液为 NaPF6 溶于 EC:EMC=3:7 至 0.8 mol/L，与候选的盐/溶剂/浓度一致；Fan 2025 也报告同一 0.8 M NaPF6/EC:EMC=3:7 体系。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec5::child0]
- NaDFP 1% 与 TMSB 1.5% 双添加剂配比（NB 电解液）：Cai 2025 将 1% NaDFP 与 1.5% TMSB 组合命名为 NB 电解液，并称 1:1.5 的 NaDFP:TMSB 比例是最适比例，正好对应候选的添加剂量。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec7][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]
- 在 -10 °C 下 NFM||硬碳软包电池的低温柔性/容量保持：Cai 2025 报告 NFM/HC 软包电池在 -10 °C、1C 下 NB 电解液的倍率性能改善，并明确含 NB 电解液的电池“更适于低温应用”，与目标电芯化学和温度一致。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3]
- 对 Al 集流体无腐蚀（阴性事实）：Fan 2025 只在电解槽/扣式电池中显示无添加剂的 NaPF6-E 几乎不与 Al 箔反应，并未测试含 NaDFP/TMSB 的 NB 电解液，也未在目标软包构型中直接观察；Cai 2025 未涉及腐蚀测试，故不能证明候选电解液对 Al 无腐蚀。 [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9::child0]
- 对不锈钢壳体无腐蚀（阴性事实）：Fan 2025 仅观察到 NaFSI-E 优先腐蚀不锈钢壳，未对含 NaDFP/TMSB 的 NaPF6 系候选电解液做壳体腐蚀观察；Cai 2025 亦无壳体腐蚀数据，缺少针对候选的直接阴性证据。 [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec9::child0]
文献与候选的关联：Cai 2025 的 NB 电解液（1% NaDFP + 1.5% TMSB）在涂覆于铝基底的 NFM 正极与硬碳负极组成的软包电池中于 -10 °C 进行评估，其盐、溶剂比、浓度和添加剂量与候选完全对应，故该文献实验可直接关联候选的低温适用性；但该实验未包含 Al 集流体或不锈钢壳的腐蚀观察，无法关联腐蚀阴性要求。 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3]

## 文献依据与已记录的计算结果
